title: Asian stocks tumble as oil surge, Fed hike bets overshadow chip optimism
full_text:
U.S. stocks end in the red as PPI boosts Fed rate hike bets, WTI crude tops $100
Investing.com -- Asian stocks fell sharply on Friday as a surge in oil prices and rising bond yields triggered a broader risk-off move, overwhelming continued strength in some artificial-intelligence stocks.
The selloff followed a fourth straight decline on Wall Street on Thursday as Brent crude pushed above $100 and Treasury yields climbed. In Asian trade, Nasdaq 100 Futures fell 0.2%, while S&P 500 Futures traded flat.
The U.S. producer price index rose 0.4% in August, while annual producer inflation accelerated to 5.4%, reinforcing expectations that the Federal Reserve could raise rates next week. Markets now price about a 70% chance of a hike.
Friday’s consumer price report will be the next major test, with investors watching whether higher energy costs are spreading into broader inflation.
Chip stocks retreat as oil shock overwhelms AI optimism
The selloff swept across Asia’s technology-heavy markets, with the broader risk-off tone overshadowing the week’s earlier gains in some chip stocks.
The MSCI Asia Pacific index fell 1.3%, while South Korea’s KOSPI dropped 2.4%, Japan’s Nikkei 225 fell 2.9% and Hong Kong’s Hang Seng lost 1.5%.
Even so, the moves left a mixed weekly picture, with the KOSPI remaining about 2.5% higher for the week, while the Nikkei was down 2.6%.
Semiconductor stocks were among the biggest casualties. South Korea’s SK Hynix fell 3.4%, though it remained about 12.7% higher on the week. Samsung Electronics lost 3.9% and was still roughly 5.3% higher over the same period.
The declines came despite continued optimism over AI-related spending, underscoring how quickly a shift in the broader macro backdrop can overshadow the sector’s growth narrative.
That pressure was even more pronounced in Japan, where Kioxia tumbled 7.8% and TDK fell 3.1%, while Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing slipped 1.43%.
The AI investment story itself, however, showed little sign of fading. Oracle shares jumped more than 6% in extended trading after the company reported stronger-than-expected cloud growth and a record $664 billion backlog, highlighting the scale of demand for AI infrastructure.
China AI chip debut bucks broader selloff
China’s Shanghai Composite fell over 2%, while Hong Kong technology stocks also weakened, with Alibaba down 0.9%, Meituan 1.1% and Tencent 0.2%.
Tencent-backed Shanghai Enflame Technology, however, surged about 200% in its Shanghai debut after raising 6.12 billion yuan ($912 million), underscoring intense investor demand for domestic AI-chip alternatives to Nvidia.
Asian government bonds also came under pressure. Australia’s three-year yield jumped to 5.05%, its highest since 2011, while New Zealand’s two-year yield rose 24 basis points. The U.S. 10-year yield climbed toward 5%.
Elsewhere, India’s Nifty 50 Futures fell 0.2% with Nifty 50 down about 1.8% this week. Singapore’s Straits Times fell 0.3%, and Indonesia’s Jakarta Composite fell 1.4%.
Australia’s S&P/ASX 200 fell 1.26%, extending its weekly decline to about 3.3%, while New Zealand’s NZX 50 dropped 0.6%
Oil remained the dominant macro risk. Brent traded around $107.66 a barrel after approaching $110, with the benchmark up nearly 13% this week.
The conflict around the Strait of Hormuz has disrupted shipping, while Iran-backed Houthi forces advanced toward Mokha near the Bab al-Mandeb Strait, raising fears of further pressure on regional energy and shipping flows.

title: Enflame shares surge 200% in Shanghai debut as AI chip frenzy intensifies
full_text:
U.S. stocks end in the red as PPI boosts Fed rate hike bets, WTI crude tops $100
Investing.com -- Shanghai Enflame Technology shares surged around 200% in their Shanghai debut on Friday, as investors piled into one of China's leading domestic AI-chip makers amid Beijing's push to reduce reliance on Nvidia and other U.S. semiconductor suppliers.
The Tencent-backed company opened at 410 yuan, well above its 142.18-yuan IPO price. The stock climbed as high as 475 yuan before trading around 430 yuan, valuing Enflame at roughly 185 billion yuan ($27.6 billion), or about three times its IPO valuation.
Enflame raised 6.12 billion yuan ($912 million) by selling 43 million new shares in the offering, which initially valued the company at about 61.2 billion yuan.
Only 4.16% of its post-IPO shares were available for trading at the debut, creating a relatively small float as demand surged. The strong debut extends a powerful run of investor enthusiasm for Chinese AI-chip companies.
Enflame's online IPO was met with orders equivalent to more than 6,000 times the shares available, while more than 7 million investor accounts participated, underscoring the appetite for companies seen as beneficiaries of China's push for domestic AI hardware.
Tencent-backed bet on China's AI-chip independence
Enflame is one of China's so-called "four little GPU dragons", alongside companies including Moore Threads, MetaX and Biren Technology.
The company develops processors and related systems for AI computing and has emerged as one of the beneficiaries of U.S. restrictions on advanced Nvidia chips and semiconductor technology exports to China.
Tencent remains Enflame's largest shareholder following the IPO, with a 17.95% stake, while it was also the company's largest end customer in 2025, accounting for 83.79% of revenue.
Enflame's revenue is growing rapidly, but the company is not yet profitable. It reported a net loss of 1.16 billion yuan in 2025, although revenue jumped 37% to 990.2 million yuan.
The IPO proceeds will be used to develop next-generation AI processors and large-scale computing systems, positioning Enflame to compete for a larger share of China's expanding AI-computing market.

title: OpenAI’s Altman considers slowing AI development amid safety concerns- Bloomberg
full_text:
U.S. stocks end in the red as PPI boosts Fed rate hike bets, WTI crude tops $100
Investing.com -- OpenAI (NASDAQ:OAI) CEO Sam Altman is considering slowing the pace of cutting-edge artificial intelligence development, potentially in coordination with other AI labs, as concerns over the safety of increasingly capable systems intensify, Bloomberg News reported Friday.
Altman discussed the possibility at a companywide meeting this week, according to people familiar with the matter cited by Bloomberg. The idea could involve several AI companies voluntarily moderating development, although some labs may not agree to such a move.
The discussion comes as safety concerns have escalated across the industry. OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki recently called for voluntary slowdowns until common safety standards are established, warning that no company can assume its safety capabilities will keep pace with increasingly powerful AI systems.
OpenAI has already taken some steps to slow development. The company said in August that it paused reinforcement-learning training on its latest models for two weeks after an incident involving an AI agent and Hugging Face, while it strengthened security, monitoring and alignment safeguards.
Its largest planned frontier reinforcement-learning run remains on hold pending further testing.
Researchers at Anthropic and Google DeepMind have also publicly raised concerns over the pace of AI development. U.S. lawmakers have now stepped up scrutiny, with the Senate investigating OpenAI's handling of the Hugging Face breach.
The debate also comes as OpenAI and Anthropic prepare for potential public listings, increasing investor focus on how the companies balance the commercial value of rapid AI progress against the costs and risks associated with developing more powerful systems.
OpenAI has separately urged Congress to establish mandatory national AI safety requirements, including independent assessments, cybersecurity measures and incident reporting.

Brent oil futures jumped 0.6% to $108.21 a barrel by 20:32 ET (00:32 GMT), while West Texas Intermediate crude futures rose 0.55% to $103.08 a barrel.

title: Samsung, Qualcomm delay 2nm chip deal as price talks drag- The Bell
full_text:
U.S. stocks end in the red as PPI boosts Fed rate hike bets, WTI crude tops $100
Investing.com -- Samsung Electronics and Qualcomm have delayed a potential contract for Samsung’s foundry business to manufacture Qualcomm’s application processors on its 2-nanometer process as the companies remain divided over pricing, The Bell reported on Friday.
The delay could push production into next year, raising questions over Samsung’s ability to secure Qualcomm as a major foundry customer even as its latest 2nm process appears to have overcome some of the performance and yield issues that previously kept the two companies from resuming cooperation.
According to the report, the two sides have not encountered major technical problems with the 2nm process currently under discussion.
Qualcomm is understood to have responded positively to the process, while Samsung’s own Exynos 2600 and upcoming Exynos 2700 chips, both based on 2nm technology, have also received favorable performance assessments.
Instead, Qualcomm is pushing for lower prices and Samsung is resisting. The negotiations have dragged on to the point that manufacturing the processors within 2026 is becoming difficult because chip production needs to line up with smartphone launch schedules.
The companies could instead shift discussions toward Qualcomm’s next-generation application processors, the report added.
The dispute highlights a change in Samsung’s foundry strategy. The business previously expanded its customer base partly by accepting lower-priced contracts, but it now appears less willing to compete on price after securing strategic customers including Tesla and Broadcom.
The production volume currently under discussion with Qualcomm is also relatively small, reducing Samsung’s incentive to make significant price concessions.
A Samsung Electronics official cited by Bell said the delay made production of the Qualcomm processors within the year difficult and that discussions around next-generation products were already being considered.
The official also said Samsung was no longer engaging in the low-price bidding it had pursued in the past after securing clients such as Tesla and Broadcom, according to the report.
Samsung and Qualcomm did not immediately respond to Investing.com’s requests for comment.

title: Japan PPI inflation beats expectations in August, stays close to 3-½ yr high
full_text:
U.S. stocks end in the red as PPI boosts Fed rate hike bets, WTI crude tops $100
Investing.com-- Japanese producer inflation slowed slightly in August but remained close to its highest level in over 3-½ years as high energy costs and a weak yen factored into rising business costs.
Producer price index inflation grew 7.6% year-on-year in August, data from the Bank of Japan showed on Friday. The print was higher than expectations of 7.4% but cooled slightly from the 7.7% print seen in July, which was revised up from 7.2%.
PPI fell 0.2% month-on-month against expectations it would remain unchanged.

While Friday’s data did show a mild cooling in producer prices, it still highlighted persistent stickiness in Japanese inflation.
PPI inflation shot up this year, underpinned chiefly by high oil and gas prices due to a prolonged U.S.-Iran war. A weak yen also added to price pressures by making imports more expensive.
A steady increase in PPI has slowly factored into higher consumer price index inflation in recent months, as businesses passed on their costs to consumers.
This in turn is expected to give the BOJ more impetus to hike interest rates. The central bank recently signaled it will discuss raising rates during its September meeting, amid growing risks from high inflation.

A 25 bps hike will bring the BOJ’s benchmark rate to 1.25%-- levels last seen in 1995. It would mark the central bank’s second such hike this year after a 25 bps raise in June.
Last week, BOJ Governor Kazuo Ueda had signaled that the central bank will discuss rate hikes during its September meeting, especially amid growing signs of sticky Japanese inflation.
Consumer price index inflation rose steadily in recent months, with the core print in sight of the BOJ’s 2% annual target.
Producer price index inflation accelerated sharply to a 3-½ year high in August, data showed on Friday, as rising energy prices and a weaker yen ramped up business costs, which are likely to be passed on to Japanese consumers.
Markets will closely watch any commentary from the BOJ on its plans for a terminal rate. Reuters reported that there is no clear consensus within the central bank on just how much rates should rise, and at what pace.
Governor Ueda is also expected to avoid committing to a specific timeframe for future hikes.

title: Gold steadies after sharp drop as hotter PPI lifts Fed hike bets
full_text:
U.S. stocks end in the red as PPI boosts Fed rate hike bets, WTI crude tops $100
Investing.com -- Gold prices were little changed on Friday after falling nearly 2% overnight, as a hotter U.S. producer price report, surging oil prices and higher Treasury yields reinforced expectations for a Federal Reserve rate hike next week.
A stronger dollar and rising Treasury yields added to the pressure ahead of the Federal Reserve’s September 14 to 15 meeting.
At 20:37 ET (00:37 GMT), XAU/USD rose 0.1% to $4,322.69 an ounce, while Gold Futures fell 1% to $4,362.87. XAG/USD was little changed at $63.57 an ounce, while XPT/USD also traded flat. The U.S. Dollar Index was little changed at 99.07.
Hotter PPI and oil revive Fed hike bets
Gold remains on track for a third consecutive weekly decline after dropping 1.8% on Thursday, its sharpest daily fall in recent weeks.
The latest pressure followed U.S. producer price data showing the index rose 0.4% in August, the strongest increase since May. The data reinforced concerns that rising energy costs are feeding into broader inflation just days before the Fed’s policy decision.
Oil has become a major part of that inflation story. Brent crude climbed close to $108 a barrel as the United States and Iran showed little sign of backing away from a prolonged conflict.
Fighting has intensified in recent weeks. The United States has struck Iranian oil tankers, Iran has launched missiles at a Jordanian airbase and Tehran backed Houthis in Yemen have attacked Saudi infrastructure.
Continued disruption to energy supplies could push inflation higher and make the Fed more likely to keep rates restrictive. Markets are now pricing roughly a 70% chance of a Fed rate hike this month.
ETF demand provides longer term support
Despite the near term pressure, gold continues to attract substantial investment demand.
The World Gold Council said global physically backed gold ETFs attracted $18 billion in August, their second largest monthly inflow on record.
Holdings increased by 121 tonnes to a record 4,189 tonnes, while assets under management jumped 16% to $615 billion.
That demand helped gold gain 13% in August, its third strongest monthly return in a quarter century, according to the World Gold Council.
Tony Sycamore, senior market analyst at IG, said gold remains well below the 200 day moving average near $4,537. The metal needs to reclaim that level to signal that the pullback from the $4,697 high is ending. Until then, he sees scope for a deeper decline toward $4,200.

title: Hong Kong court jails two Tiananmen vigil group leaders for 7 years
full_text:
U.S. stocks end in the red as PPI boosts Fed rate hike bets, WTI crude tops $100
By Joyce Zhou
HONG KONG, Sept 11 (Reuters) - A Hong Kong court sentenced two pro-democracy activists to seven years in prison on Friday, after they were convicted for inciting subversion, with judges highlighting their use of the phrase "end one-party dictatorship" in their political activities.
Lee Cheuk-yan, 69, and Chow Hang-tung, 41, were part of a group that organised annual vigils marking Beijing’s 1989 Tiananmen Square crackdown on pro-democracy protesters.
Public commemorations of the 1989 protests used to be legal and tolerated in Hong Kong and were seen as a symbol of the city’s relative freedoms compared to mainland China. They were effectively outlawed in 2020 when the National Security Law came into force following mass protests the year before.
Lee and Chow, the former chair and former vice-chair of the now-disbanded Hong Kong Alliance in Support of Patriotic Democratic Movements of China, have been in custody since 2021.
Lee was sentenced to seven years, while Chow was sentenced to seven years and three months after being convicted last month under the national security law.
They had pleaded not guilty.
Another former chairman of the group and also a former chairman of the city’s largest opposition Democratic Party, Albert Ho, 74, pleaded guilty in January.
He was sentenced to five years and two months in jail.
The Hong Kong Alliance faces a fine of HK$1.5 million ($191,304), the court judgement said.
Lawyers for Lee, Chow and Ho were not immediately available for comment.
Prosecutors had argued the primacy of the Communist Party was enshrined in Article 1 of the Chinese constitution. Defence submissions that the defendants genuinely believed they were acting within the law given Hong Kong’s freedoms of speech were rejected by the judges.
"By severely punishing the activists for conducting ordinary democratic activities, the Hong Kong High Court has violated their rights to freedom of expression and peaceful assembly," said Elaine Pearson, Asia director at Human Rights Watch.
($1 = 7.8409 Hong Kong dollars)

title: Five big takeaways from Trump’s midterm convention
full_text:
U.S. stocks end in the red as PPI boosts Fed rate hike bets, WTI crude tops $100
By Tim Reid
Sept 10 (Reuters) - President Donald Trump and his Republican Party wrapped up an unusual convention in Dallas on Thursday hoping to strengthen their midterm election prospects, gambling that a high-profile show of party unity will energize supporters and help Republicans defy historical midterm losses.
Here are five takeaways from the two-day convention.
RUNNING AGAINST A ’SOCIALIST HELLSCAPE’
The Republican National Committee had billed the convention as a chance to refocus voters on Trump’s political agenda and tout the party’s policy successes.
But Trump and many other speakers on the convention stage focused most of their time on attacking Democrats as left-wing extremists and dangerously un-American. U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent accused Democrats of wanting to turn the country into a "socialist hellscape."
The tactic of attacking political opponents and injecting fear into an election campaign is a strategy deployed by both parties for decades. Trump has long made issues such as crime and immigration central to his political appeal.
The focus on Democrats underscored the political challenges confronting Republicans as they seek to defend their congressional majorities. With dissatisfaction over high prices and the war in Iran weighing on Trump, speakers repeatedly argued that Democratic control of Congress would pose the greater risk.
IT’S THE ECONOMY, STUPID
The gathering took place against the backdrop of growing unhappiness over Trump’s stewardship of the economy and his inability to bring down high prices on gasoline and groceries.
Trump has been under pressure from White House aides since last year to talk more about the economy. Yet as he has done for months, Trump said little about the pain Americans are experiencing from the high cost of living.
Instead, he said concerns about inflation were exaggerated, after a summer in which opponents say he has appeared more focused on renovation and legacy projects in Washington including his White House ballroom.
In his Wednesday night speech Trump again said that the word "affordable" was "fake" and that it was Democrats who caused high prices.
"I’m bringing prices way down," Trump said, a statement that jars with government economic data.
Trump and other speakers did tout his 2025 tax cuts, which led to larger refunds from the tax-collecting Internal Revenue Service this year for many families, and his efforts to reduce drug prices.
’PRETEND THAT I’M ON THE BALLOT’
Trump and many Republicans believe that his MAGA supporters are less likely to vote when he is not on the ballot, as will be the case in November.
"Pretend that I’m on the ballot," Trump said to cheers. But Democratic strategists may well have had more reason to celebrate, viewing his determination to put himself at the center of the campaign as advancing their effort to make the election a referendum on an unpopular president.
Trump’s strategy is a gambit that risks turning off critical swing voters needed to win congressional races but who have drifted away from Trump and his party over a range of issues, including the economy, the war and immigration raids.
BIG-TICKET PROMISES
Trump used the speech to make several ambitious promises, some of which may be difficult to deliver.
The most extraordinary was a proposal to pay every U.S. adult a $5,000 "Trump dividend" if Republicans win the elections and retain their control of both houses of Congress.
The proposal faces the same obstacle as Trump’s previously floated $2,000 tariff rebate, which never won congressional approval: persuading lawmakers to support a measure that could cost more than $1 trillion.
Trump also promised that oil prices would drop "as soon as we win the war with Iran," which he predicted would end "right after Election Day," November 3.
The conflict has shown little sign of ending since the U.S. and Israel launched strikes on Iran in February, frustrating Trump’s efforts to bring it to a close either through military pressure or diplomatic negotiation.
POSSIBLE START OF JD VANCE’S PRESIDENTIAL CAMPAIGN
If Republicans lose one or both chambers of Congress in November, it will likely intensify a simmering debate over who will succeed Trump as the party’s presidential candidate in 2028. A central figure in that discussion is Vice President JD Vance.
On Thursday night, Vance delivered a keynote address that offered a glimpse of how he might position himself should he seek the presidency. While embracing Trump’s populist politics and combative attacks on Democrats, he devoted far more time to themes of family, faith and children’s futures than Trump typically does, casting the election as a fight to preserve what he called Americans’ "birthright."
Vance was greeted by chants of "48, 48" – a reference to the idea he could be the 48th U.S. president after Trump, the 47th. "We got to take care of business this November, then we’ll worry about what comes next," he said.
A key unknown is whether Trump will eventually anoint a successor, and the president gave no hint of his thinking when he took the stage after Vance. His endorsement could carry enormous weight after a decade in which he reshaped the party and built a fiercely loyal base of supporters.

The U.S. dollar index was around 99.06, little changed after rising 0.3% on Thursday to its highest level since September 7. The EUR/USD pair was flat at 1.1609, while the GBP/USD pair rose 0.06% to 1.3520.

Brent crude rose 1.2% to $108.96 a barrel in early Asian trading, extending a six-day rally as renewed Middle East tensions raised concerns about energy supply disruptions.
Dollar gains support as Fed hike bets rise
U.S. producer prices rose 0.4% in August, in line with expectations, according to data released on Thursday. Energy prices rebounded during the month, adding to concerns that higher oil prices could keep inflation elevated.
Markets are now awaiting U.S. consumer-price data later Friday, one of the final major releases before the Federal Reserve’s September 15-16 meeting.
Fed funds futures were pricing a 71.3% probability of a 25-basis-point rate hike, up from 61.2% in the previous session, according to CME Group’s FedWatch tool. A hotter-than-expected CPI reading could further strengthen the dollar by reinforcing expectations for tighter policy.
DBS said its baseline is for the Fed to remain at 3.75% at the September meeting, but highlighted the meeting as potentially contentious, with market pricing leaning toward a hike.
The rise in U.S. yields has also kept pressure on global bond markets. The 10-year Treasury yield was around 4.97% early Friday, close to the 5% level, according to Reuters.

The yen recovered some ground after Japan’s wholesale inflation data showed prices rose 7.6% year-on-year in August, faster than economists had expected. The data reinforced expectations that the BOJ will raise rates next week.
The BOJ is widely expected to lift its policy rate by 25 basis points to 1.25% at its September 17-18 meeting.
DBS similarly expects a 25-basis-point hike but sees the BOJ signaling a flexible pace of tightening rather than committing to rapid successive increases.
That leaves the yen sensitive to both the BOJ’s guidance and the Fed’s decision, particularly after the USD/JPY pair’s sharp decline over the past month.
Asian currencies mixed ahead of data-heavy week
Other Asian currencies showed mixed weekly moves. The USD/AUD pair is up about 0.6% this week, implying a weaker Australian dollar, while the New Zealand dollar has strengthened recently.
The USD/CNH and USD/CNY pairs were broadly flat on the week.
The USD/SGD pair was also largely unchanged, while the USD/KRW pair was little changed despite a stronger won in Friday trading.
The USD/INR pair was around 95.67 after the rupee came under pressure from the surge in oil prices this week.
Next week brings several important Asia data releases. India is due to report August CPI, exports and imports on Monday.
China’s August retail sales, industrial production and fixed-asset investment are due on Tuesday, followed by Japan’s August trade data on Wednesday.

title: ECB policymakers open door to more rate hikes on energy risk
full_text:
U.S. stocks end in the red as PPI boosts Fed rate hike bets, WTI crude tops $100
By Francesco Canepa and Balazs Koranyi
FRANKFURT, Sept 11 (Reuters) - Two European Central Bank policymakers opened the door on Friday to further interest rate increases if a war-fuelled rise in energy prices continues and pushes up other prices in the euro zone.
The ECB raised borrowing costs on Thursday for the second time this year and sources told Reuters policymakers expect further policy tightening in the months ahead, with a move possible as early as October.
The central bankers of Germany and Estonia acknowledged this prospect on Friday although they both stressed any move would depend on how oil and gas prices develop.
Bundesbank President Joachim Nagel said the ECB might need to raise rates to a level that mildly curbs the economy.
"I will not exclude that we have to go into the mild restrictive territory, but as I said, it’s very much dependent on how the energy prices evolve, how the price picture is evolving over the course of maybe the next month," he told CNBC in an interview.
The euro zone central bank increased its key rate from 2.25% to 2.50%, bringing it to the upper end of its estimated neutral range, which neither stimulates nor slows down the economy.
Money markets have started pricing in at least another three ECB rate hikes over the next year.
Ülo Kaasik, Estonia’s central bank governor, said such expectations were "understandable" given the latest increase in fuel prices and the risk that food would also become more expensive.
"Recent developments in energy markets, for example, indicate the possibility that the price increase for gas and fuels will be much larger and last longer than expected in the forecast," he said in a blog post.
Slovenia’s central bank governor Primož Dolenc also warned in a blog post about "rising energy and electricity costs in the autumn and winter months".
The ECB on Thursday slightly increased its projections for growth and inflation but these did not capture the latest energy price moves.

title: Austrian central bank says economic outlook improving, to be felt next year
full_text:
VIENNA, Sept 11 (Reuters) - Austria’s central bank has trimmed its economic growth forecast for the country in 2026 due to a weaker-than-expected first six months of the year, but raised it for next year as the outlook is improving, it said on Friday.
In an update to its last economic forecasts published in June, the Austrian National Bank (OeNB) said it now expects gross domestic product to grow by 0.5% this year, 0.1 points less than it had previously predicted. It raised its forecast for 2027, however, to 1.3% from 1.1%.
"Despite the war in the Middle East and this summer’s drought, the economic outlook for the second half of 2026 has improved," the ONB said in a statement.
"Global trade grew more strongly than expected, which should also benefit the Austrian export sector. At the same time, the order-book situation and sentiment in the domestic manufacturing sector have improved," it said, adding that the effects of those would mainly be felt next year.
The central bank trimmed its forecast for Austrian inflation according to the Harmonised Index Of Consumer Prices (HICP) to 3% this year from 3.2%, and to 2.3% next year from 2.4%.

title: French economy not in danger but deficit must be cut, central bank chief says
full_text:

PARIS, Sept 11 (Reuters) - French central bank chief Emmanuel Moulin said on Friday that France was not in catastrophic economic danger but the government must act to reduce the country’s public deficit.
Moulin was speaking after INSEE revised its economic forecast for the euro zone’s second-largest economy lower on Thursday, predicting growth of just 0.4% this year. Moulin cited several factors such as a deadly heatwave and issues at Airbus.
France’s national statistics institute previously forecast growth of 0.7% for 2026, short of last year’s 0.9% expansion.
"I wouldn’t say it (the economy) is in danger, but it is in a situation that’s worrisome and unsatisfactory," Moulin told RTL radio.
"We need to reduce the budget deficit. But beyond that, the French economy has its strengths. It has inexpensive energy and a diversified economy. We’re seeing an industrial upturn across promising sectors such as data centres, defence, and aerospace. So the situation isn’t entirely catastrophic," he added.
The French government is expected to lower its own growth forecast, currently at 0.7%, on Friday as it prepares to send its 2027 budget bill to parliament at the end of the month.
